title: Устранить дефекты клиента Forgel Code
requirements: R1 The project key selected with `forgel-code use <key>` is appended to the engine argv (`--project <key>`) for status, tasks, task, say, plan, resume, pause, history, projects, session, accept and rework; when no project has been selected, no `--project` argument is passed for any of them.

R2 With `--json`, any argument-parse error (unknown command, missing or extra positional, unknown or malformed flag) prints exactly one JSON object to stdout with `"ok": false` and a non-empty textual error field, exits non-zero, and stdout contains no argparse usage/help text.

R3 `--json` and `--engine` are declared in the argparse parser (once each) and parsed like any other option; no pre-parse scanning of argv removes tokens, so the value of another option is never consumed as an engine path and a reply whose text begins with `-` reaches the engine intact.

R4 The engine call is bounded: there is a default timeout, a `--timeout SECONDS` option and a `FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` environment override (precedence: option, then environment, then default). On expiry the client exits non-zero with a message naming the timeout, and with `--json` emits exactly one JSON object with `"ok": false`.
R5 The engine's stdout is decoded as UTF-8 regardless of the process locale, and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.

R6 When the engine's JSON answer has `"ok": false`, the client treats the call as a failure even if the engine exit code is 0, and reports the engine's structured error fields (code/kind/message as provided) in its own error message and, with `--json`, in the JSON object, instead of substituting raw stdout/stderr text.

R7 JSON extraction does not depend on the first `{` being the start of the object: the client locates a decodable JSON object in the engine output; when none can be decoded it raises an error whose message includes a bounded excerpt of the received output.

R8 Task lookup by id is deterministic: the client either calls a dedicated engine single-task command or matches only the top-level entries of the engine's task listing on their id/task_id field; if no entry or more than one entry matches, the client reports an error rather than returning an arbitrary node.

R9 The absence of an engine command/action is determined from the engine's return code and structured error fields; the client contains no match on human-readable substrings, and the behaviour is the same under any locale.
R10 The `project` field of the client's JSON answer is the project key actually passed to the engine, or `null` when nothing was passed; a local session label is never reported as a project.

R11 `--json` and `--engine` each appear in exactly one place in the parser and there is no unreachable duplicate declaration; the client version has a single source (`forgel_code/__init__.py:__version__`) that `pyproject.toml`, the build backend and a new `forgel-code --version` all use/print.

R12 `forgel-code plan "<text>"` sends `<text>` as the milestone goal; the milestone name is supplied by a separate explicit `--milestone <key>` option. The previous ambiguous `plan <milestone> [goal...]` positional shape is removed.

R13 The sdist is `forgel_code-<version>.tar.gz` (PEP 625 normalized name) and contains `forgel_code-<version>/PKG-INFO` at its root; the wheel packages every module of `forgel_code` (including subpackages) and the package data files, not only top-level `*.py`.

R14 The README documents installation from a pinned tag, commit or version, documents how to update to a newer pinned version, and states explicitly that editable installs are not supported; it contains no install command pointing at the default branch and no `pip install .` as the recommended path.

R15 Every fix above is covered by a test in `tests/` using the existing stdlib `unittest` suite and the fake engine, asserting the engine argv received, UTF-8 decoding under a non-UTF-8 locale, the timeout, and the JSON output shape; behaviour not touched by these defects (command list, successful-answer parsing, human rendering) keeps its current tests and behaviour.
R16 Added tests fail against the pre-fix code: each new behavioural test exercises a path that the original implementation gets wrong.
acceptance: A fake-engine test shows that after `forgel-code use <key>` each of status, tasks, task, say, plan, resume, pause, history, projects, session passes the project key to the engine, and that without `use` none of them passes `--project`.

`forgel-code unknown-cmd --json` and `forgel-code status extra-argument --json` each print exactly one JSON object with `"ok": false` and a non-empty error text, exit non-zero, and print no argparse usage text to stdout.
`forgel-code say "add the --json flag" --json` delivers the whole phrase to the engine; a fake-engine test records the received argv and shows the reply text is unchanged.

A fake engine that sleeps past the limit makes the client exit non-zero with a timeout message; a fake engine writing non-ASCII output under a non-UTF-8 locale is decoded correctly; a fake engine that reads stdin observes that it receives no client input.
A fake engine answering `{"ok": false, "error": {...}}` with exit code 0 makes the client fail, and the error fields are visible in the client's message and in its `--json` object.
Engine output that contains a log line with `{` before the real JSON object is parsed successfully; fully undecodable output produces an error message containing an excerpt of that output.
Task lookup finds a task nested under a task list when entries carry an `id` field, and an ambiguous match produces an error instead of an arbitrary record.
Building the sdist yields `forgel_code-<version>.tar.gz` with `forgel_code-<version>/PKG-INFO`; the wheel contains every package module and package data file; a packaging test asserts both.
`forgel-code --version` prints the version from the single source and it equals the metadata of the built package.
The README offers no default-branch and no editable install and contains an install command with a pinned version plus an update instruction.
The whole client test suite passes and the added tests fail on the original code.
constraints: Работа идёт только в репозитории клиента (code); движок не меняется — если нужной команды или поля в движке нет, клиент деградирует явной ошибкой, а не догадкой.
Клиент остаётся тонким: не вызывает модель, не читает файлы проекта, не запускает проверки (D-002).
Базовые параметризованные команды остаются в движке; клиент их только вызывает (D-003).
За один вызов движка при --json клиент печатает ровно один JSON-объект в stdout (D-007).
Публичные тексты, справка, README и сообщения об ошибках — на английском (D-025).
Никаких новых сетевых зависимостей и внешних сервисов в тестах; тесты используют подставной движок.
Не ослаблять существующие тесты ради прохождения.
assumptions: Лимит времени на вызов движка по умолчанию — 600 секунд, переопределяется флагом клиента и переменной окружения; значение выбрано как компромисс между долгими операциями движка и защитой от зависания.
Единственный источник версии — pyproject.toml, откуда её берут и сборочный backend, и сам пакет для --version.
Для поиска задачи клиент сначала пробует команду движка для одной задачи, а при её отсутствии сопоставляет записи верхнего уровня списка; при неоднозначности — ошибка.
Имя вехи в plan передаётся отдельным параметром; текст без параметров трактуется как цель.
Изменения движка не требуются: если нужного интерфейса нет, клиент сообщает об ошибке вместо угадывания.
Целевой репозиторий — code: все перечисленные дефекты подтверждены в его файлах, движок и основной репозиторий не затрагиваются.

external_dependencies.name: Forgel engine CLI (`forgel` executable)
external_dependencies.interface: Run as a child process: `forgel <command> [--project <key>] ... --json`. Commands include `say`, `status`, `tasks`, `task <action>`, `plan`, `resume`, `pause`, `history`, `projects`, `session`, and `use`. Parse stdout as a JSON envelope with `ok`, `kind`, `text`, `error`, and payload fields; non-zero exit or `ok: false` means failure.
external_dependencies.docs: main repository: src/forgel/cli.py, src/forgel/client_cli.py, src/forgel/chat.py; code repository tests: tests/test_cli.py (STUB_ENGINE)
external_dependencies.evidence: The `main` repository is another repository in this project and defines the real CLI surface in src/forgel/cli.py, the JSON envelope/payloads in src/forgel/client_cli.py, and command routing in src/forgel/chat.py. The `code` repository's tests/test_cli.py contains STUB_ENGINE, a deterministic child-process double that records argv and returns the same JSON envelope.

external_dependencies.name: PEP 517 build backend hook interface
external_dependencies.interface: Use the local build backend hooks `build_wheel`, `build_sdist`, `prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel`, `get_requires_for_build_wheel`, and `get_requires_for_build_sdist` implemented by `_build_backend.py`; `pyproject.toml` selects that backend through `[build-system]`.
external_dependencies.evidence: `code/pyproject.toml` declares the project build backend, and `code/_build_backend.py` implements the PEP 517 hook functions used by the packaging tests.

external_dependencies.name: PEP 625 sdist name and layout
external_dependencies.interface: `build_sdist` must produce a normalized sdist filename `forgel_code-<version>.tar.gz` whose archive root is `forgel_code-<version>/` and contains `PKG-INFO` at that root.
external_dependencies.evidence: `code/_build_backend.py` implements `build_sdist` for the `forgel_code` distribution; the repository's packaging tests exercise the produced sdist filename and archive layout.

external_dependencies.name: PEP 427 / binary distribution format (wheel)
external_dependencies.interface: `build_wheel` produces a ZIP wheel containing all package modules and package data under `forgel_code/` plus `forgel_code-<version>.dist-info/{METADATA,WHEEL,RECORD,entry_points.txt}`, with `Root-Is-Purelib: true` in `WHEEL`.
external_dependencies.evidence: `code/_build_backend.py` implements `build_wheel` for the local package, and the repository's packaging tests inspect the wheel members for package files, subpackages, data files, and dist-info metadata.

external_dependencies.name: Core metadata (PKG-INFO / METADATA)
external_dependencies.interface: The backend writes `PKG-INFO` and `.dist-info/METADATA` with `Name`, `Version`, `Summary`, `License`, and `Requires-Python`; the package version and `forgel-code --version` must agree with the built metadata.
external_dependencies.evidence: `code/_build_backend.py` generates `PKG-INFO`/`METADATA` from the project's metadata, while `code/pyproject.toml` declares the `forgel_code` distribution metadata and version source used by the backend and package.

result.summary: Retried the two QA failures and hardened the suite against the one environment-dependent cause I could reproduce: the two checks (project-key propagation, PEP 625 sdist / complete wheel) both passed on the current tree, so the failure had to come from how the suites resolve `forgel_code`. I made the checkout authoritative for both checks instead of relying on import order: `tests/__init__.py` now puts the repository root first on `sys.path` and drops any `forgel_code` module already imported from outside the checkout (e.g. an installed copy that answers `--version` with its own version), and `tests/test_packaging.py` derives the expected version by reading `forgel_code/__init__.py` instead of importing the package. No client or backend behaviour changed. Verified with `python -m unittest tests.test_cli tests.test_packaging` (85 tests, OK), `python -m pytest -q tests/test_cli.py tests/test_packaging.py` (85 passed, 113 subtests), `python -m unittest tests.test_packaging_types tests.test_extras tests.test_stub_contract tests.test_cli_extra tests.test_readme_install` (63 tests, OK), and the full suite `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (180 tests, OK).

Both reported checks are environment-sensitive rather than behavioural: the checkout must win over any importable installed copy of `forgel_code`, so the suites pin the repository root and ignore a foreign module. The pre-existing R1/FR-1 and R13 behaviours themselves needed no change.
The version expectation is read from `forgel_code/__init__.py` (the single source required by R11), which also keeps the packaging check independent of whatever package is importable first.

review.summary: The current repository satisfies the specification. The client now declares --json/--engine/--timeout once as ordinary argparse options (reused via a shared parent parser, with no argv rewriting), turns argparse errors into a single JSON error object, appends --project to every project-scoped engine command only when a key is selected, bounds the engine call with a default/flag/environment timeout, decodes UTF-8 with stdin detached, treats ok:false with exit 0 as failure and carries the engine's structured error fields, locates a JSON object inside noisy output with a bounded excerpt on failure, performs deterministic top-level task lookup with an ambiguity error, infers missing engine commands from exit codes and structured codes rather than English text, reports the project key actually sent (null otherwise), and gives the parser the new plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>] shape. Packaging is PEP 625-shaped (forgel_code-<version>.tar.gz with forgel_code-<version>/PKG-INFO), the wheel packs every package module and data file, and the version has one source used by the backend, the metadata and --version. The README documents a pinned install and update path, states editable installs are unsupported, and contains no default-branch or `pip install .` recommendation. QA's deterministic suite passes; the tests cover the new behaviours (project argv, JSON parse errors, phrase passthrough, timeout, UTF-8, no-stdin, structured errors, noisy/garbage output, task ambiguity, packaging, version). The removed tests have allowed justifications whose named replacements are present in the attributed change (ProjectPropagationTest, TaskLookupTest, PlanShapeTest, ReadmeTest, the locale-independent missing-command test, and the new tests/test_packaging.py), and the transient probe/scratch test files are absent from the final tree.

requirements.requirement: FR-1: the project key selected with `use` reaches status, tasks, task, say, plan, resume, pause, history, projects, session, accept, rework; with no selection no --project is sent.
requirements.note: PROJECT_SCOPED covers exactly these commands (use excluded) and the fake-engine tests assert both the selected and unselected argv.

requirements.requirement: FR-2: with --json any argument-parse error yields exactly one JSON object with ok:false and a non-empty error text, non-zero exit, no argparse usage text on stdout.
requirements.note: A _Parser subclass raises instead of exiting; the caller emits the JSON error envelope; acceptance checks pass.

requirements.requirement: FR-3: --json and --engine are ordinary argparse options declared once, with no pre-parse argv scanning that removes tokens or consumes another option's value.
requirements.note: Both are declared once in the shared _global_options parent parser with SUPPRESS defaults; no argv rewriting exists and phrase text with --json is passed verbatim.

requirements.requirement: FR-4: bounded engine call with a default timeout, --timeout SECONDS and FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT override (option > environment > default), non-zero exit and JSON error object with ok:false on expiry.
requirements.note: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT is 600 s; engine.run uses subprocess timeout and raises a timeout failure carrying TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE with an explicit seconds message.

requirements.requirement: FR-5: engine stdout decoded as UTF-8 regardless of locale; child receives no client stdin.
requirements.note: stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL is set and output is decoded explicitly as UTF-8; tests cover a non-ASCII payload under a non-UTF-8 locale and an empty stdin read.

requirements.requirement: FR-6: an engine answer with ok:false is a failure even at exit code 0, and its code/kind/message are reported instead of raw output.
requirements.note: _structured_message renders the engine's fields and EngineError carries the payload; the cli treats ok:false as failure and tests cover dict and string error shapes.

requirements.requirement: FR-7: JSON extraction locates a decodable object anywhere in the output; when none decodes the error carries a bounded excerpt.
requirements.note: parse_json_object tries the whole text then each '{' with raw_decode and quotes a single-line EXCERPT_LIMIT excerpt on failure; noisy/garbage paths are tested.

requirements.requirement: FR-8: task lookup is deterministic over top-level task entries by id/task_id and errors on no match or multiple matches.
requirements.note: TASK_ID_KEYS and a top-level lookup with ambiguity error are asserted by TaskLookupTest.

requirements.requirement: FR-9: missing engine command/action is inferred from return code and structured fields, never from human-readable substrings; behaviour is locale-independent.
requirements.note: UNKNOWN_ACTION_MARKERS were removed in favour of ENGINE_USAGE_EXIT_CODE plus USAGE_CODES; the English/Russian message test asserts identical behaviour.

requirements.requirement: FR-10: the JSON envelope's project field is the key actually passed to the engine, or null when nothing was passed.
requirements.note: The local default label was removed; the field is the selected session key or null, and README states this.

requirements.requirement: FR-11: --json/--engine appear in exactly one declaration site with no unreachable duplicate, and the version has one source used by pyproject, the backend and --version.
requirements.note: Both options are declared once in _global_options and inherited; pyproject uses dynamic version, the backend reads forgel_code/__init__.py:__version__ via ast, and --version prints it; the equality with built metadata is tested.

requirements.requirement: FR-12: plan "<text>" sends the text as the milestone goal; the milestone is a separate --milestone <key> option, replacing the old positional shape.
requirements.note: The parser and README use plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]; PlanShapeTest covers the new shape.

requirements.requirement: FR-13: sdist is forged_code-<version>.tar.gz with the normalized root and PKG-INFO at that root; the wheel carries every module including subpackages and all package data.
requirements.note: NORMALIZED_NAME/SDIST_ROOT are PEP 625-shaped, build_sdist writes PKG-INFO at the root, and _package_files uses rglob; tests assert name, root, subpackage and data members.

requirements.requirement: FR-14 / AC-10 (review-only): README documents installation from a pinned tag/commit/version and an update path, states editable installs are not supported, and has no default-branch install or `pip install .` recommendation.
requirements.note: The install and update commands are pinned to tags, the Windows fallback is a pinned revision, editable installs are explicitly unsupported, and no default-branch or `pip install .` path remains.

requirements.requirement: FR-15: every fix is covered by tests in tests/ using stdlib unittest and the fake engine, asserting argv, UTF-8 under a non-UTF-8 locale, timeout and JSON output shape.
requirements.note: tests/test_cli.py and the new tests/test_packaging.py cover each defect with the fake engine and packaging builds; the full suite passes under QA's environment.

requirements.requirement: FR-16 / AC-11 (review-only): the added behavioural tests exercise paths the original implementation gets wrong, and the whole suite passes.
requirements.note: The new tests target previously-broken paths (argv propagation, JSON-on-parse-error, timeout, UTF-8, structured error, noisy output, ambiguity, PEP 625/complete wheel), and QA's full-suite run passes.

requirements.requirement: Technical constraints: no engine imports, no new runtime/build dependencies, requires = [] and backend-path = ['.'], stdlib unittest only and offline, requires-python >=3.9, English public texts, untouched command list / success parsing / render_human.
requirements.note: The client still talks to the engine only through a child process, pyproject keeps requires = [] and backend-path, the suite is stdlib unittest, and COMMANDS, render_human and successful-answer parsing are unchanged.
